Current nets enter A/input 0, previous nets B/input 1; both streams have unique ascending net identifiers, which form the Join key. NewNetChecks is wired to output 0, MeshReview to output 1, RetiredNetChecks to output 2. A seed bank compares the previous container census on A/input 0 with the replacement census on B/input 1. Write complete DataIntersection CTL, not a graph-wide script. Identifiers are unique and ascending; Join key $container=$container, default error actions. Send shared containers to CropChanges only when crop differs, preserving literal old/new values. RemovalReview reads output 0 and ultimately needs reason=NOT_IN_CENSUS, but its first edge must contain the original old-container rows. Output 2 feeds ContainerRegistration with the incoming rows unmodified. Output 1 feeds CropChanges. Include any placement advice needed for the removal reason.

Layouts (! required, ? nullable): A(container:string!, crop:string?); B(container:string!, crop:string?); output 1 (container:string!, old_crop:string?, new_crop:string?).

Write the complete DataIntersection component CTL for a fabric-roll inventory reconciliation. Current rolls enter input 0 (A); the previous inventory enters input 1 (B), with a unique ascending roll key in each feed. CurrentOnlyIntake receives output 0, RetiredRollAudit receives output 2, and QualityComparison receives output 1; both one-sided consumers require their source rows unaltered. QualityComparison needs every shared roll, current weave and grade, and changed=true if either tracked value differs. Unknown weave and blank weave differ; identical nulls agree. Join by roll.

Input A fields: roll:string!, weave:string?, grade:integer!. Input B fields: roll:string!, weave:string?, grade:integer!. Reconciliation consumer fields: roll:string!, weave:string?, grade:integer!, changed:boolean!. A question mark marks nullable fields; ! marks required fields.

Generate the entire CTL2 implementation for an instrument-tuning DataIntersection. The previous readings are A/input 0, current readings B/input 1; instrument is the unique ascending join identity. All three consumers are wired: MissingInstrumentReview on output 0, TuningDelta on output 1, and AddedInstrumentReview on output 2. Missing and added reviews need their respective input records unchanged. Report every shared instrument with changed and current-minus-previous adjustment; adjustment is null if either reading is unknown, while changed compares unknown as distinct from any number. No error action override is configured.

Layouts (! required, ? nullable): A(instrument:string!, cents:integer?); B(instrument:string!, cents:integer?); output 1 (instrument:string!, changed:boolean!, adjustment:integer?).

An art-print studio needs full DataIntersection CTL, including its entry functions. Input A is proof samples, input B master samples; grouping identity is job, with ascending job order and duplicate keys allowed. Compare every proof against every master of the same job, returning BOTH, INK, DPI or NONE according to its ink and resolution differences. Preserve null as an actual state. ProofOnlyArchive is connected to output 0, InspectionPairs to output 1, MasterOnlyArchive to output 2; the archives expect the original one-sided records. Every candidate pair must be represented in InspectionPairs.

Layouts (! required, ? nullable): A(job:string!, proof:string!, ink:string?, dpi:integer?); B(job:string!, master:string!, ink:string?, dpi:integer?); output 1 (job:string!, proof:string!, master:string!, discrepancy:string!).

Write the Normalizer CTL2 for this complete event-posting policy.

For payroll attendance segments, choose the earliest eligible treatment below. Every treatment lists its complete ordered payload.

[unfinished attendance] eligibility: clock_out equals null; result: OPEN {minutes=0, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=null, paid=false}.
[withdrawn sheet] eligibility: category equals "CANCEL"; result: no postings.
[backward clock] eligibility: duration < 0; result: ERROR {minutes=duration, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration minutes, paid=false}.
[approval pending] eligibility: not approved; result: PENDING {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=false}.
[training attendance] eligibility: category equals "TRAIN"; result: TRAIN {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.
[three travel segments] eligibility: category equals "TRAVEL" and duration >= 60; result: OUTBOUND {minutes=30, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 30 minutes, paid=false}; then ONSITE {minutes=duration-60, segment_from=clock_in plus 30 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration-30 minutes, paid=true}; then RETURN {minutes=30, segment_from=clock_in plus duration-30 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration minutes, paid=false}.
[overtime allocation] eligibility: net > 450; result: REGULAR {minutes=450, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 450 minutes, paid=true}; then OVERTIME {minutes=net-450, segment_from=clock_in plus 450 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.
[reviewed work] eligibility: review; result: AUDIT {minutes=0, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 0 minutes, paid=false}; then WORK {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.
[ordinary paid work] eligibility: otherwise; result: WORK {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.

Measure duration as whole elapsed minutes between the clock timestamps; subtract break_minutes for net, using zero for an absent break. OPEN has no ending timestamp. Travel outbound and return are unpaid commuting, while onsite is paid. Other complete sheets satisfy 0 <= break_minutes <= duration; the backward-clock rule covers negative intervals.

Input 0 Source_time_2: sheet_id / required / string; clock_in / required / date; clock_out / nullable / date; break_minutes / nullability omitted / integer; approved / required / boolean; review / required / boolean; category / nullable / string.
Output 0 Posting_time_2: source_sheet_id / required / string; pay_bucket / required / string; minutes / required / long; segment_from / required / date; segment_to / nullable / date; paid / required / boolean.
Source sheet_id values are unique. Preserve each in source_sheet_id on its postings.

Provide complete Normalizer CTL2 for the posting policy below.

Build event expansion for the voucher and cash tender accounting feed, applying the first matching test. Keep listed postings in order.

1) For void receipt (payment_status equals "VOID"), the event produces nothing.
2) For invalid voucher (voucher < 0), the event produces ERROR valued at -voucher.
3) For reservation (payment_status equals "RESERVE"), the event produces RESERVE valued at sale_value.
4) For refund (payment_status equals "REFUND"), the event produces REFUND valued at -sale_value.
5) For reviewed split tender (sale_value > voucher and voucher > 0 and review), the event produces VOUCHER valued at voucher, then CASH valued at sale_value-voucher, then AUDIT valued at 0.
6) For voucher overpayment (voucher > sale_value), the event produces VOUCHER valued at sale_value, then CHANGE valued at voucher-sale_value.
7) For mixed tender (voucher > 0), the event produces VOUCHER valued at voucher, then CASH valued at sale_value-voucher.
8) For cash only (none of the preceding conditions applies), the event produces CASH valued at sale_value.

Input 0 (In_voucher_tender_2): external_tender_id = string; accepts null: no | sale_value = decimal; accepts null: no | review = boolean; accepts null: no | payment_status = string; accepts null: no | voucher = decimal; accepts null: no | tender_note = string; accepts null: yes.
Output 0 (Out_voucher_tender_2): parent_tender_ref = string; accepts null: no | tender_leg = string; accepts null: no | value = decimal; accepts null: no | allocation_key = long; accepts null: no.
Each source ID is unique; carry external_tender_id into parent_tender_ref. Entry labels go in tender_leg, values in value. Every nonsilent event receives a fresh allocation_key shared by its postings. Sequence Keys_voucher_tender: long, start 3000000000, step 1, reset for this run; silent events consume no key.

1. unfinished attendance: clock_out equals null. Emit OPEN {minutes=0, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=null, paid=false}.

Emit OUTBOUND {minutes=60, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 60 minutes, paid=true}; then ONSITE {minutes=duration-120, segment_from=clock_in plus 60 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration-60 minutes, paid=true}; then RETURN {minutes=60, segment_from=clock_in plus duration-60 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration minutes, paid=true}.
7. overtime allocation: net > 480. Emit REGULAR {minutes=480, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 480 minutes, paid=true}; then OVERTIME {minutes=net-480, segment_from=clock_in plus 480 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.
8. reviewed work: review. Emit AUDIT {minutes=0, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 0 minutes, paid=false}; then WORK {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.
9. ordinary paid work: otherwise. Emit WORK {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.

duration is the whole elapsed minutes from clock_in to clock_out; net subtracts break_minutes, treating a missing break as zero. Dates are UTC. 7. simultaneous earn and spend: earned > 0 and redeemed > 0. Emit EARN {delta=earned, remaining=balance+earned, valid_until=expires_on, needs_review=false}; then SPEND {delta=-redeemed, remaining=balance+earned-redeemed, valid_until=expires_on, needs_review=false}; then BALANCE {delta=0, remaining=balance+earned-redeemed, valid_until=expires_on, needs_review=false}.

9. remaining movement: otherwise. Emit SPEND {delta=-redeemed, remaining=balance-redeemed, valid_until=expires_on, needs_review=false}.

## Practice task (component type: REFORMAT)

Legal services returns processing in India: write a Reformat for returned court-filing packets. Retain rows where clearance_granted is true OR return_reference is non-null and starts with "RTN-IN-". A null return_reference does not satisfy the prefix condition.

Copy return_reference. Set handling_lane to bulk when document_delta is at least 10, otherwise routine. Enrich retained rows using document_delta:
- direction_tag: decrease for negative, unchanged for zero, increase for positive.
- volume_class: reconciliation for negative, empty for zero, light for 1..9, moderate for 10..19, heavy for 20..39, escalated from 40.
- queue_rank: assign 9/0/1/2/3/4 to those volume classes in that order.
- audit_needed: true for negatives or at least 40, otherwise false.
- next_step: reconcile_manifest for negative, supervisor_check from 40, otherwise process_return.
- bounded_documents: clamp document_delta to 0..40.
- bundle_parity: even or odd according to document_delta.

Return the complete CTL2 code.

## Practice task (component type: NORMALIZER)

Sports and entertainment subscription invoices in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland receive fee revisions sorted by subscription reference, then strictly increasing billing-effective time. Each subscription uses one fixed currency, EUR or CHF.

Write a one-output Normalizer that emits zero or one delta per revision. Emit each subscription's first revision. Thereafter, emit only when the fee changes between unknown and known, or when the absolute difference between the incoming fee and the last emitted fee is at least 0.01 currency units. Two unknown fees produce no delta. Compare decimal values directly without rounding.

Retain the last emitted fee and its billing-effective start; ignored revisions must not update this state. Thus, several individually small revisions can eventually trigger a delta relative to the last emitted fee. Unknown fees differ from zero. The import timestamp is nullable audit information only and must not shift billing validity. A subscription reference can be an empty string.

Input InvoiceRevision(subscription_ref:string!,fee_value:decimal?,imported_at:date?,billing_effective_at:date!). Output InvoiceFeeDelta(contract_ref:string!,initial_revision:boolean!,prior_fee:decimal?,prior_billing_start:date?,revised_fee:decimal?,billing_start:date!,audit_timestamp:date?).

Populate contract_ref from subscription_ref, revised_fee from fee_value, billing_start from billing_effective_at, and audit_timestamp from imported_at. Set initial_revision to true only for the first revision of each subscription. For subsequent emitted revisions, prior_fee and prior_billing_start come from the last emitted revision. Both prior fields are null for the first revision.

Write the settlement accounting export for banking claims processed in Serbia, in the Balkans. All monetary amounts are in Serbian dinar minor units (para). Listed rules have precedence from top to bottom. Parentheses give the exact value for each named entry.

1. withdrawn claim: when case_stage equals "WITHDRAWN", export nothing.
2. invalid insurance allocation: when insurer_allocation < 0, export ERROR (-insurer_allocation).
3. pending assessment: when case_stage equals "ASSESSMENT", export nothing.
4. reversed settlement: when case_stage equals "REVERSED", export REVERSAL (-assessed_loss).
5. compliance review: when compliance_check is true and either evidence_reference is absent or assessed_loss > insurer_allocation, export HOLD (assessed_loss) followed by AUDIT (0). An absent evidence_reference means null, not an empty string.
6. excess insurance allocation: when insurer_allocation > assessed_loss, export INSURER (assessed_loss) followed by EXCESS (insurer_allocation-assessed_loss).
7. shared settlement: when insurer_allocation > 0, export INSURER (insurer_allocation) followed by BANK (assessed_loss-insurer_allocation).
8. bank-funded settlement: otherwise, export BANK (assessed_loss).

Input 0 (In_banking_claim_0): case_number stores a long value; must be present
assessed_loss stores a long value; must be present
compliance_check stores a boolean value; must be present
case_stage stores a string value; must be present
insurer_allocation stores a long value; must be present
evidence_reference stores a string value; may be absent.
Output 0 (Out_claim_accounting_0): claim_reference stores a long value; must be present
posting_category stores a string value; must be present
posting_amount stores a long value; must be present.
Each source ID is unique; carry case_number into claim_reference. Entry labels go in posting_category, values in posting_amount. Emit entries in the order specified by the first matching rule.

Implement the following airline dispatch mapping for Andean-region services.

Copy dispatch_ref. Trim departure_day_text; null/empty is MISSING, an invalid strict yyyy-MM-dd date in UTC is INVALID, otherwise VALID with canonical yyyyMMdd. The canonical value is null unless valid. Use locale es.PE.

Normalize origin_iata by trimming and uppercasing. origin_check is MISSING for blank, INVALID unless exactly three characters, OK otherwise. Typical origins include BOG, UIO, LIM, and LPB.

airtime_check is MISSING when planned_airtime_min is null, INVALID when <=0, OK otherwise.

Determine reserve_class from planned_airtime_min and fuel_endurance_min:
- MISSING if either value is null.
- INVALID if either value is <=0.

Null dispatcher_release means false. Count one problem for each of: a non-VALID departure date, a non-OK origin, a non-OK airtime, a MISSING/INVALID/BELOW_MINIMUM reserve class, and a false release. These checks count independently, even when one missing input affects multiple checks.

Set dispatch_lane to HOLD when any problem exists; otherwise EXTENDED_RESERVE when reserve_class is EXTENDED, and READY otherwise.

## Practice task (component type: REFORMAT)

An Andean food and beverage fraud-detection service reviews declared prices for Peruvian quinoa beverages in PEN per litre. Records are sorted by producer and inspection time. A Reformat must carry the accepted price between consecutive records, restarting its state for each producer and each new calendar day.

Input metadata (port 0):
- producer_registry: long, non-nullable
- inspected_at: date, non-nullable
- declared_pen_per_litre: decimal, nullable

Output metadata (port 0):
- reviewed_registry: long, non-nullable
- reviewed_at: date, non-nullable
- accepted_pen_per_litre: decimal, nullable
- declaration_accepted: boolean, non-nullable

Write CTL2 code that emits one output record per input record and applies these rules:

- Copy producer_registry to reviewed_registry and inspected_at to reviewed_at.
- Always accept the first record of a producer or calendar day, even if declared_pen_per_litre is null.
- Otherwise, reject a null declaration. Accept a non-null declaration if the carried accepted price is null or the absolute difference from that price is no more than PEN 2 per litre.
- On acceptance, replace the carried price with declared_pen_per_litre. On rejection, leave it unchanged.
- Output the carried price as accepted_pen_per_litre and indicate whether the current declaration was accepted in declaration_accepted.

Use calendar dates in the America/Lima time zone when detecting day changes. How should the transformation distinguish an uninitialized state from a legitimately null accepted price, and reset that state when either the producer or calendar day changes?

A mining returns processor in Kazakhstan receives successive revisions of the declared mass of returned copper concentrate, measured in metric tonnes. For each return case, sum only the positive increases between successive known mass declarations: when the current known mass exceeds the previous known mass, add their difference; decreases and unchanged values contribute zero. Missing declarations are ignored and do not replace the previous known mass.

The first known declaration establishes the baseline and sets the accumulated increase to zero. If every declaration is missing, the accumulated increase must remain null. Also report whether that accumulated increase is non-null.

A group consists of adjacent records with equal return_case_ref. Process records in arrival order. Suppress groups containing only one source record; retain groups containing two or more source records, including records with missing declarations. Include the source-record total in revision_total. Number only emitted groups from one in this run and include that ordinal in settlement_sequence.

Input:
ConcentrateReturnInput
- return_case_ref (string): required
- declared_tonnes (decimal): allows null

Accumulator:
ConcentrateReturnState
- revisions_seen (long): required
- prior_tonnes (decimal): allows null
- upward_tonnes (decimal): allows null

Output 0:
ConcentrateReturnSummary
- return_case_ref (string): required
- revision_total (long): required
- added_tonnes (decimal): allows null
- settlement_sequence (long): required
- has_declaration (boolean): required

Supply the complete Rollup and a brief explanation.

Produce automotive loyalty campaign summaries for a dealership network in Morocco, North Africa. Use a Rollup grouped by campaign_code, with adjacent groups processed in input order.

Input LoyaltyActivity(campaign_code:string non-nullable, member_code:string, posted_on:date, earned_points:long, membership_state:string).

Accumulator metadata is fixed at LoyaltyAccumulator(points_sum:decimal, eligible_rows:long); all metadata listed here is final.

Output LoyaltyCampaignSummary(campaign_code:string non-nullable, opening_member:string, closing_member:string, opening_year:integer, closing_year:integer, qualifying_count:long, absent_points_count:long, invalid_points_count:long, premium_count:long, suspended_count:long, lowest_points:decimal, highest_points:decimal, combined_points:decimal, average_points:decimal, campaign_status:string, member_trace:string).

Save the first and last member_code, including null, and the UTC calendar years of their posted_on values; a null timestamp yields a null year.

Classify membership_state as PREMIUM, SUSPENDED or other using exact, case-sensitive matching; null belongs to other. Count PREMIUM and SUSPENDED activities regardless of their earned_points.

An activity qualifies for qualifying_count, lowest_points, highest_points, combined_points and average_points only when earned_points is non-null and nonnegative AND membership_state is not SUSPENDED. Set campaign_status to HOLD whenever suspended_count is positive, even without qualifying activities. Otherwise set it to EMPTY without qualifying activities, REVIEW when any points are missing or negative, and READY otherwise.

1. withdrawn: when transaction equals "WITHDRAW", export nothing.

8. inception: when otherwise, export BIND (premium).

Build the payroll attendance segments Normalizer using these ordered business decisions. Stop at the first applicable policy.

1. unfinished attendance: clock_out equals null. Emit OPEN {minutes=0, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=null, paid=false}.
2. withdrawn sheet: category equals "CANCEL". Emit no postings.
3. backward clock: duration < 0. Emit ERROR {minutes=duration, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration minutes, paid=false}.
4. approval pending: not approved. Emit PENDING {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=false}.
5. training attendance: category equals "TRAIN". Emit TRAIN {minutes=duration, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration minutes, paid=true}.
6. three travel segments: category equals "TRAVEL" and duration >= 120. Emit OUTBOUND {minutes=60, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 60 minutes, paid=true}; then ONSITE {minutes=duration-120, segment_from=clock_in plus 60 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration-60 minutes, paid=true}; then RETURN {minutes=60, segment_from=clock_in plus duration-60 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus duration minutes, paid=true}.
7. overtime allocation: net > 480. Emit REGULAR {minutes=480, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 480 minutes, paid=true}; then OVERTIME {minutes=net-480, segment_from=clock_in plus 480 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.
8. reviewed work: review. Emit AUDIT {minutes=0, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus 0 minutes, paid=false}; then WORK {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.
9. ordinary paid work: otherwise. Emit WORK {minutes=net, segment_from=clock_in plus 0 minutes, segment_to=clock_in plus net minutes, paid=true}.

duration is the whole elapsed minutes from clock_in to clock_out; net subtracts break_minutes, treating a missing break as zero. Dates are UTC. Segment boundaries use clock_in plus the listed minute offsets; the segment_to of OPEN is absent. Negative net is allowed only by the explicit ERROR treatment; other complete sheets have break_minutes between zero and duration.

```xml
<Record name="PolicyEffectiveFilled" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter="|" recordDelimiter="\n" nullValue="__NULL__">
  <Field name="policy_no" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="effective_at" type="date" nullable="false" format="yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" timeZone="UTC"/>
</Record>
```

```ctl
//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    $out.0.policy_no = $in.0.policy_no;
    $out.0.effective_at = nvl($in.0.effective_at, zeroDate);
    return ALL;
}
```

## Practice task (component type: NORMALIZER)

Durum-wheat procurement quotes from cooperatives in Tunisia arrive as a change log sorted by procurement agreement, then strictly increasing applicability time. Prices are in Tunisian dinars per tonne.

Write a one-output Normalizer that emits zero or one record per input event. Emit each agreement's first event. Thereafter, emit an event when its quoted price differs from the last accepted price OR at least seven complete 24-hour periods have elapsed since the last accepted event's applicability time. This allows unchanged quotes to refresh periodically. Suppressed events must not update the retained state.

Retain the last accepted price and applicability time for comparison and for populating the previous-version fields. Unknown price differs from zero; two unknown prices count as equal. The logging timestamp is optional audit information only: missing or delayed logging must not shift validity. An agreement can have an empty string key.

Input WheatQuote(agreement_ref:string!,quoted_tnd:decimal?,logged_at:date?,applies_at:date!). Output ProcurementRevision(agreement_ref:string!,initial_quote:boolean!,prior_tnd:decimal?,prior_since:date?,quoted_tnd:decimal?,binding_since:date!,logged_at:date?).

Populate binding_since from applies_at. Set initial_quote to true only for an agreement's first emitted event, and set both prior fields to null for that event. For subsequent emissions, populate the prior fields from the last accepted event. Copy agreement_ref, quoted_tnd, and logged_at from the current input.

## Practice task (component type: JOIN)

Write the transform for manufacturing incident response monitoring at factories in Bangladesh, South Asia. A contains permitted response times and B contains measured response times, not chronological snapshots. For each matched incident, emit its identifier, permitted response time, measured response time, and whether the permitted time was exceeded.

Record layouts:
- A: incident_ref (string, required); permitted_minutes (integer, required)
- B: incident_ref (string, required); elapsed_minutes (long, required)
- Middle result: incident_ref (string, required); permitted_minutes (integer, required); elapsed_minutes (long, required); response_overdue (boolean, required)

A/input 0 contains incident-specific response limits; B/input 1 contains measured minutes from incident reporting to the maintenance team's first response. Each incident appears once in each feed where present, and both feeds are sorted ascending incident_ref. Join key $incident_ref=$incident_ref. Physical outputs 0=A-only, 1=both, 2=B-only are connected.

For matched incidents on output 1, set response_overdue to true only when elapsed_minutes is greater than permitted_minutes; otherwise set it to false. Copy the other matched fields to the middle result.

## Practice task (component type: NORMALIZER)

Sports and entertainment subscription invoices in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland receive fee revisions sorted by subscription reference, then strictly increasing billing-effective time. Each subscription uses one fixed currency, EUR or CHF.

Write a one-output Normalizer that emits zero or one delta per revision. Emit each subscription's first revision. Thereafter, emit only when the fee changes between unknown and known, or when the absolute difference between the incoming fee and the last emitted fee is at least 0.01 currency units. Two unknown fees produce no delta. Compare decimal values directly without rounding.

Retain the last emitted fee and its billing-effective start; ignored revisions must not update this state. The import timestamp is nullable audit information only and must not shift billing validity. A subscription reference can be an empty string.

Both prior fields are null for the first revision.

Set dispatch_lane to HOLD when any problem exists; otherwise EXTENDED_RESERVE when reserve_class is EXTENDED, and READY otherwise.

Set dispatch_lane to HOLD when any defect exists; otherwise TOP_UP for SHORT deliveries, SURPLUS for EXCESS deliveries, and RELEASE otherwise.

7. joint consultation settlement: when booking_state equals "JOINT", export CLINIC (consultation_fee*30/100) followed by PRACTITIONER (consultation_fee*(100-30)/100).
